Covariate screening on individual PK estimates before modelling

Source: R/nm_suggest_run.R
nm_suggest_covariates.Rd

Applies the Wasserstein-distance comparison of nm_wasserstein() to the individual estimates obtained by nm_suggest_model() (NCA clearance, central volume and absorption parameter of the rich intervals, log scale), before any NONMEM run. For each covariate, subjects are split into groups (each level against the first for a categorical covariate; Q4 against Q1, or all pairs of quartiles, for a continuous one) and the distributions of the log estimates are compared with the 1-Wasserstein distance, a permutation test and a Welch t-test. It points to covariates worth testing in the model; it is no substitute for the covariate model (individual NCA estimates carry their own estimation noise, and only subjects with a rich interval are used).

Usage

nm_suggest_covariates(
  x,
  covariates,
  data = NULL,
  parameters = c("CL", "Vc"),
  n_perm = 2000L,
  seed = 2025L,
  max_levels = 5L,
  continuous = c("extremes", "pairwise")
)

# S3 method for class 'nm_suggest_covariates'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An nm_model_suggestion object (individual estimates are needed, i.e. at least 3 rich intervals).

covariates

Character vector of covariate columns.

data

Covariate data (data.frame or CSV path with an ID column). Default: the dataset analysed by nm_suggest_model().

parameters

Individual estimates to analyse among "CL", "Vc", "KA", "DUR", "MTT" (default c("CL", "Vc")).

n_perm

Number of permutations (default 2000).

seed

Random seed of the permutation tests; the user's random state is restored.

max_levels

A numeric covariate with at most this many distinct values is treated as categorical (default 5).

continuous

"extremes" (Q4 vs Q1, default) or "pairwise".

...

Ignored.

Value

A data.frame of class nm_suggest_covariates: parameter, covariate, type, comparison, n_1, n_0, ratio_median (median of group 1 / median of group 0), W, p_W, p_t, p_W_adj (Bonferroni over the comparisons of a covariate and parameter).

References

Simon N, Hulot JS, von Fabeck K. Distribution-based covariate assessment using Wasserstein distance in population pharmacokinetic models. Front Pharmacol. 2026;17:1804989. doi:10.3389/fphar.2026.1804989

See also

nm_suggest_model(), nm_wasserstein()

Examples

ex <- system.file("extdata", "example", "example_data.csv", package = "nmpilot")
s <- nm_suggest_model(ex, verbose = FALSE, design_eval = FALSE, max_profiles = 15)
nm_suggest_covariates(s, covariates = c("WT", "GENO"), n_perm = 500)
#> Covariate screening on individual estimates (log scale, Wasserstein distance)
#>  parameter covariate        type comparison n_1 n_0 ratio_median     W   p_W
#>         CL        WT  continuous   Q4 vs Q1   3   4        0.834 0.255 0.902
#>         Vc        WT  continuous   Q4 vs Q1   3   4        1.309 0.404 0.084
#>         CL      GENO categorical     1 vs 0   2  13        1.577 0.428 0.070
#>         Vc      GENO categorical     1 vs 0   2  13        0.949 0.185 0.932
#>    p_t p_W_adj
#>  0.596   0.902
#>  0.111   0.084
#>  0.438   0.070
#>  0.952   0.932
